items.alt: Opposite charges +2.0 and −3.0 microcoulombs, 0.50 m center to center, attract with equal 0.216 N forces.
A positive and negative point charge attract; equal inward force arrows show 0.216 N on each charge.
Charges +2.0 and −3.0 microcoulombs are separated by 0.50 m measured between their centers.
Equal inward arrows show each charge experiences the same attractive force, approximately 0.216 N.
Doubling both charge magnitudes and halving center-to-center separation increases force sixteenfold, from 0.216 N to about 3.45 N.
Original and changed charge pairs compare 0.50 m and 0.25 m separations and the resulting sixteenfold force increase.
Electrons move from initially neutral object B to object A; protons stay in the material.
Object A gains electrons transferred from object B, which loses electrons.
Equal and opposite net charges: A has −0.32 microcoulombs and B has +0.32 microcoulombs.
Electron gain makes A negative; electron loss makes B positive, with equal charge magnitudes.
An isolated-system boundary surrounds A and B. Their −0.32 and +0.32 microcoulomb charges add to zero.
After electron transfer, A and B have equal opposite charges and the isolated system retains zero total charge.
A proton and electron attract through both electric and gravitational interactions at the same separation r. Arrows indicate direction only.
Both electric and gravitational forces attract the proton-electron pair. The two models use the same separation.
Identical separation r appears in both models, so the inverse-square distance terms cancel in their force ratio.
Electric and gravitational attractions act on the same proton-electron pair; arrows show direction rather than comparative strength.
Cutaway model of neutral matter shows equal positive and negative charge, explaining why large-scale electric effects can cancel.
Both interactions attract the same particle pair at separation r; the electric-to-gravitational force ratio is independent of that common distance.
Three charges lie in a line: +3.0 microcoulombs left, −2.0 middle, +5.0 right, at separations of 0.40 m and 0.50 m.
Opposing forces act on the negative middle charge: attraction left toward Q1 and right toward Q3. The schematic is not to scale.
Q1 attracts Q2 leftward with force approximately 0.337 N over a 0.40 m separation.
Q3 attracts Q2 rightward with force approximately 0.360 N over a 0.50 m separation.
The rightward attraction slightly exceeds the leftward attraction, giving a net force of 0.0225 N right on Q2.
Signed addition of the opposing electric forces gives 0.0225 N to the right on the middle charge.
